messages:
sylvia: FYI PD started firing around 06:12 UTC for the cache layer, looks like a cascade of identical alerts. lots of pages. i'm pausing my morning to triage. :coffee:
incident-bot: INCIDENT ALERT • service/cache-layer • 06:12 UTC • 480 alerts in 4m • pd: critical • link: https://redwood.internal/incidents/2120001234
raj: i'm seeing a spike in 503s coming from the shared prefix cache. traffic burst + cold misses. frontend latency also ticked up to 2.2s for a subset of p99 routes.
michael: on it. can someone post which alert rule is flapping?
raj: rule name = cache_backend_5xx_rate_high (prometheus). fingerprint looks identical across alerts => likely same root cause.
sylvia: customer impact: rough estimate 0.8% of requests returned 503s over a 10m window, concentrated on batch inference jobs. one paying customer reported timeouts via support.
ops-ryan: i'm going to gateway the PD noise: creating an immediate temporary silence for non-actionable duplicates + rate-limit on slack notifications. will update PD schedule after.
julie: +1. we should avoid clearing alerts entirely, we want a dedupe/grouping approach not blind silence.
raj: propose quick mitigations: 1) Alertmanager dedupe by fingerprint + group_interval = 5m 2) Add `for: 1m` to the prom rule to avoid flapping on short bursts 3) Temporary PD suppression for alerts where error-rate < 1% for last 10m
michael: agreed. drafting the change now. sample alertmanager changes i plan to apply (dry-run first):
```yaml
route:
  group_by: ['fingerprint', 'alertname']
  group_wait: 30s
  group_interval: 5m
  repeat_interval: 3h
  receiver: 'pd-pager'
receivers:
  - name: 'pd-pager'
    pagerduty_configs:
      - service_key: $PD_KEY
        severity: '{{ if eq .CommonLabels.severity "critical" }}critical{{ else }}warning{{ end }}'
```
raj: also a prometheus tweak to the rule (temporary):
```yaml
- alert: cache_backend_5xx_rate_high
  expr: sum(rate(cache_5xx_total[2m])) by (instance) > 50
  for: 1m
  labels:
    severity: warning
  annotations:
    description: "High 5xx spike on cache instance {{ $labels.instance }}"
```
sylvia: can we add a rate-limit on Slack channel notifications? currently every alert posts a message + threads get spammed. i had to mute my phone. :grimacing:
ops-ryan: yes - will flip the channel integration to bundle notifications for this route. PD will still page per rule but slack gets grouped.
julie: for post-incident: we should add a dashboard slice showing "alert fingerprint count" and a histogram of alerts per 5m window to spot floods. linking to ops dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/ops/alerts-overview
michael: noted. after this incident i will: 1) push the alertmanager group_interval change to staging 2) update the prom rule with `for: 1m` 3) add a recording rule to compute `alert_fingerprint_count` 4) open a PR for a new grafana panel
raj: regarding PD routing: can we route duplicates to a low-noise escalation path (pagerduty: second-tier) so SRE isn't paged for every duplicate? maybe route based on `severity` + `fingerprint_count`?
sylvia: i like that. product impact alerts (errors affecting customers >0.5%) should always page primary. background infra flaps go to a secondary path.
ops-ryan: i've created a temporary PD escalation policy and applied a silence for non-customer-impacting instances. PD silence id: S-2120-xyz (expires in 2h).
incident-bot: SILENCE CREATED • id=S-2120-xyz • expires=2h • created_by=ops-ryan
michael: i'm rolling the config to staging now. will monitor for regressions. if we see missed legitimate pages, i will rollback immediately.
julie: reminder for the postmortem/triage doc: include timeline, customer impact, changes made, follow-ups (dashboards + alert thresholds + PD routing). i'll own the follow-ups doc.
sylvia: handoff: i need to head to customer sync at 07:15. @raj can you take on-call primary until 08:30?
raj: taking it. i'll keep an eye and escalate back to michael if anything spikes.
ops-ryan: after we finish the config push, i'll create a ticket to add a rate-limit + bundle setting to the slack integration so future floods don't spam channels.
michael: post-incident checklist (quick):
- [x] temporary PD silence for duplicates
- [x] group_interval applied in alertmanager (staging)
- [x] prom rule `for: 1m` added (staging)
- [ ] add alert fingerprint panel to ops/grafana
- [ ] PR for PD routing by fingerprint_count
- [ ] retrospective note in #incidents with impact numbers
raj: i ran a quick query to quantify impact:
```
sum(increase(requests_total{status=~"5.."}[10m])) / sum(increase(requests_total[10m]))
```
result ~ 0.008 => ~0.8% failed. attaching link: https://grafana.redwood/d/query/2120001234
sylvia: thanks. please file a follow-up issue for tuning the threshold to reduce noise but keep customer-safety. julie, i'll ping you with support ticket ids for the affected customer.
julie: got it. i'll own the customer comms once we finalize the incident summary.
ops-ryan: final note: for immediate noise reduction we used two levers: dedupe (grouping by fingerprint) + rate-limit (bundle notifications). long term we should add an automated "burst mode" that temporarily raises `for:` and increases grouping when a flood pattern is detected. i'll open a design ticket.
michael: agreed. any objections to making the alertmanager group_interval default 5m for infra alerts?
raj: fine with me. ops-ryan, can you coordinate a rollback plan if this hides anything critical?
ops-ryan: yes — rollback documented in the runbook (link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/alerting-rollback).
sylvia: thanks team. handing off now. i'll update the incidents channel with a short summary and link to the follow-up ticket. :white_check_mark:
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE • status=monitoring • impacted_customers=1 • pct_errors=0.8% • followup_ticket=INC-2120001240
raj: taking over. i'll post any new alerts here and escalate as needed.
